en: The Archimedes screw uses a helical surface inside a cylinder to lift water, demonstrating the inclined plane simple machine.
The Shanghai Maglev train uses magnetic levitation to eliminate track friction, allowing it to travel at speeds over 400 kilometers per hour.
The Moon's gravitational pull is only one-sixth as strong as Earth's, causing astronauts to bounce when walking on its surface.
Neodymium magnets, made from an alloy of neodymium, iron, and boron, are currently the strongest type of permanent magnets available.
The electric eel, scientifically named Electrophorus electricus, can generate a massive shock of up to 860 volts to stun its prey.
The James Webb Space Telescope uses eighteen gold-coated beryllium mirrors to collect and focus faint infrared light from distant galaxies.
The sperm whale produces clicks reaching 230 decibels, making it the loudest animal on Earth, loud enough to vibrate a human body.
The Tiwi-MakBan geothermal power plant in the Philippines harnesses underground thermal energy from volcanoes to generate clean electricity.
The Magat Dam in the Philippines converts the kinetic energy of flowing water into electrical energy using large spinning turbines.
The Voyager 1 spacecraft continues moving through interstellar space due to inertia, requiring no fuel to maintain its constant velocity.
The Kingda Ka roller coaster in New Jersey possesses maximum gravitational potential energy when its train reaches the top of the launch tower.
The Philippine eagle uses the aerodynamic force of lift generated by its wide wings to soar effortlessly above the forest canopy.
